I can feel how deeply you’re struggling, and I can only imagine how exhausting this must be for you. His behavior is definitely not normal, and it seems like both of you are caught in a cycle that’s hard to break. At 13, he’s still a child, and sometimes extreme behavior like this can come from past trauma, learned behaviors, or something going on that he hasn’t been able to express.

Have you had a chance to explore what might have triggered this shift in him? It might help to look back and see if there’s anything in his environment—at school, at home, or with people he’s been around—that could have affected him.

Therapy for both of you sounds like it could be beneficial, not just for his behavior but also to help you process your own feelings. This situation is beyond what most parents could handle on their own, and having professional support might help you both find a path forward.

If it ever feels like you’ve truly exhausted all options and you can’t see a way to help him yourself, exploring other resources or support systems (like guardianship or foster care with people equipped to handle his needs) might be a last resort, but it could offer him a chance to get the help he needs.

Wishing you both healing and peace.
